test_title: SSC Selection Post Graduation Level Official Paper (Held on: 8 Feb 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following festivals is NOT observed on a full moon day?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Eid-al-Fitr**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eid-Ul-Fitr**

 
 
• **Eid-Ul-Fitr **marks the end of the holy month of **Ramadan** and is celebrated by the Muslim community across the globe.
 
• **It starts the day after the observation of the crescent moon, which usually occurs one night after the new moon**.
 
• Eid-Ul-Fitr, also known as** Meethi Eid, marks the end of Roza (fast),** which is observed during the whole month of Ramadan.
 
• On Eid-Ul-Fitr, Muslims thank Allah for offering them health and resistance during Ramadan.
 
• This festival is observed on the first day of **Shawwal** - the month that comes after Ramadan in the Hijri calendar.
 
• Additionally, the beginning of any lunar Hijri month varies according to the new moon sighting by religious authorities.
 
• And since Eid Ul-Fitr also marks the first day of Shawwal month, it is celebrated on different days across regions.
 
• Muslims also observe Eid-Ul-Adha, which follows soon after Eid Ul-Fitr.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shab-e-Barat**

 
 
• Shab-e-Barat a major celebration for the Muslim community is also known as the night of fortune and forgiveness. 
 
• Shab e-Barat takes place on the** full moon** and the date of the public holiday in Bangladesh
 
 
 
• **Buddha Jayanti**
 
 
• According to Buddhist legends, Buddha was born as Prince Siddhartha Gautama on the Baisakh full moon day in 563 BC at Lumbini in Nepal.
 
• His birth anniversary is also known as Vaisakhi Buddha Purnima or Vesak.
 
• The **full moon day, **Buddha Purnima is the most sacred day for Buddhists.
 
 
 
• **Rakshabandhan**
 
 
• According to the Hindu calendar, the holy festival of Raksha Bandhan is celebrated on the** full moon **day of Shukla Paksha of Shravan month.
 
• The holy festival of Rakshabandhan is a symbol of the love of brother and sister.
